pending_commit.commit_message: dev-lang/python: disable bluetooth USE flag Upstream gentoo introduced a new 'bluetooth' IUSE for installing some required bluez headers. Setting this USE flag adds bluez as a DEPEND to the python ebuild. Unfortunately, this creates a circular dependency: (dev-cpp/gtest-1.8.0-r1:0/0::portage-stable) depends on (dev-lang/python-2.7.15:2.7/2.7::chromiumos) (buildtime) (net-wireless/bluez-5.44-r186:0/0::chromiumos) (buildtime) (chromeos-base/libchrome-462023-r5:462023/462023::chromiumos) (buildtime) (dev-cpp/gtest-1.8.0-r1:0/0::portage-stable) (buildtime) However, disabling this USE flag just restores state to what it was before this USE flag was created, and since everything was already working, it should continue to work with the USE=-bluetooth. The 'bluetooth' USE flag is currently set globally in make.defaults, but we can use package.use.mask to disable for just python, and also ensure that this doesn't get overridden by later overlays (jetstream). Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:736313 TEST=PreCQ and SDK tryjob Change-Id: I6c13d18265c1f2b313479e3e768506416549ca7f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626179 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Manoj Gupta <manojgupta@chromium.org>

CRAS: audio_thread - Ignore next_cb_ts of draining streams In the current version, when a stream is draining and there are some samples in a share memory, we will wake up at the next_cb_ts of that stream. However, if a device is full, we can not take out all samples from the stream. Meanwile, the next_cb_ts is not updated because the stream is draining. It causes the audio thread always wake up at that next_cb_ts and trigger busy loop. To fix this problem, we can ignore next_cb_ts if the streams is draining. The first reason is we don't need to fetch that stream any more. The second reason is a device already have its own wake up time, which is the time that a device needs more samples. So we don't need to worry about that these samples will not be played. (see cras_iodev_frames_to_play_in_sleep) BUG=chromium:958492 TEST=Do not trigger busyloop when device buffer is full. (Tested on eve by seting incorrect rate in cras.) tast-tests: shill_stability: ask Upstart for PID The logic we use for determining the shill PID is complicated and can be much more easily done by simply asking Upstart what it thinks the PID is. This also fixes a subtle race condition: if a previous job has recently re-started shill, shill may not have finished fork()/execve() yet, and so a 'pgrep shill' will not find it yet. We could try to hack around this by modifying the shill Upstart job to report 'started' later, but really this is just a fact of life of many Upstart services -- the 'started' state does not necessarily mean everything is fully "up and running." BUG=none TEST=run back to back with, e.g., network.ConfigureServiceForProfile TEST=hack this job to run shill.Safe{Stop,Start}() first Change-Id: I40ebbfbbbae19f0254a787614ca693d8c0405fbd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1647537 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: arm64: perf: Fix callchain parse error with kernel tracepoint events For ARM64, when tracing with tracepoint events, the IP and pstate are set to 0, preventing the perf code parsing the callchain and resolving the symbols correctly. ./perf record -e sched:sched_switch -g --call-graph dwarf ls [ perf record: Captured and wrote 0.146 MB perf.data ] ./perf report -f Samples: 194 of event 'sched:sched_switch', Event count (approx.): 194 Children Self Command Shared Object Symbol 100.00% 100.00% ls [unknown] [.] 0000000000000000 The fix is to implement perf_arch_fetch_caller_regs for ARM64, which fills several necessary registers used for callchain unwinding, including pc,sp, fp and spsr . With this patch, callchain can be parsed correctly as follows: ...... + 2.63% 0.00% ls [kernel.kallsyms] [k] vfs_symlink + 2.63% 0.00% ls [kernel.kallsyms] [k] follow_down + 2.63% 0.00% ls [kernel.kallsyms] [k] pfkey_get + 2.63% 0.00% ls [kernel.kallsyms] [k] do_execveat_common.isra.33 - 2.63% 0.00% ls [kernel.kallsyms] [k] pfkey_send_policy_notify pfkey_send_policy_notify pfkey_get v9fs_vfs_rename page_follow_link_light link_path_walk el0_svc_naked ....... shill: stop forcing low bitrates during association/configuration This code was somewhere between a workaround and a real fix -- it's probably a better maintenance model to fix up a device's rate control algorithm, rather than specify exactly which rates it should use. For one, forcing low rates can directly conflict with some enterprise configurations, which explicitly try to steer clients toward only higher rates (to help budget airtime). Additionally, we can run into situations where the Basic Rates advertised by an AP don't overlap with the rates we've forced here (noticed to some extent in https://crbug.com/886529) -- and the result is that drivers tend to just ignore the request we're making here entirely. We've already fixed up the one driver that (we think) was driving the adoption of this feature in the first place (ath9k) to use a better rate control algorithm, so hopefully we're not losing out on anything. We may want to loosen up (or drop entirely) the network_WiFi_LowInitialBitrates Autotest, although to some extent it may still be valid: we expect drivers not to jump to extremely high bitrates too quickly, or else they may have reliability issues. shill: make upstart job 'expect fork' It's nice if, when our Upstart job reaches the 'started' state, we can expect there to be a shill process on the system. This is particularly helpful for tests like Tast's network.ShillStability, which can run very quickly after a test that restarts shill. I noticed problems here when running tast run ${HOST} network.ConfigureServiceForProfile network.ShillStability This significantly tightens that race, but it doesn't completely resolve it -- there's a tiny window between when minijail0 forks and when it exec's shill. So 'started shill' may still briefly show only a minijail0 process.
